description: A study of how an office receives, records, processes, stores and supplies information, including office types, staff, equipment, filing, mail handling and modern office technology.

mcq.questionText: What is the main work performed by an office in a business organisation?

options.text: Receiving, recording, processing, storing and supplying information

mcq.explanation: An office is the centre of an organisation where information is received, recorded, processed, stored and later supplied to those who need it.

mcq.questionText: Which type of office has one large room where all staff work together without separating walls?
mcq.explanation: An open-plan or general office is a single large room shared by many workers, while a cellular office uses small separate rooms.

mcq.questionText: Which office machine is mainly used to make many copies of a document quickly?
mcq.explanation: A photocopier reproduces several copies of an original document quickly, saving time compared with copying by hand.

mcq.questionText: In filing, arranging documents according to the letters of the alphabet (A to Z) is known as which method?
mcq.explanation: Alphabetical filing arranges records by the names of persons, firms or subjects in A to Z order, for example Asha, Baraka, Juma.

mcq.questionText: Which member of office staff is normally the first person a visitor meets when entering the office?
mcq.explanation: The receptionist receives visitors, finds out their needs and directs them to the right officer, giving the first impression of the organisation.

mcq.questionText: A franking machine in an office is used mainly to:

options.text: Print impressions of postage on envelopes instead of using stamps

mcq.explanation: A franking machine prints a postage mark directly on envelopes, removing the need to stick postage stamps and speeding up outgoing mail.

mcq.questionText: Filing letters according to the dates on which they were written or received is called:
mcq.explanation: Chronological filing arranges documents in order of date, with the most recent usually placed in front.

mcq.questionText: Which method of filing arranges records according to towns, regions or countries, such as Dar es Salaam, Mwanza and Arusha?
mcq.explanation: Geographical filing groups documents by location, useful for a firm with branches or customers in different regions.

mcq.questionText: The section of an office responsible for receiving, recording and distributing incoming and outgoing mail is called the:
mcq.explanation: The registry or mailing department handles all incoming and outgoing correspondence and keeps records of letters received and sent.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following is an advantage of an open-plan office over a cellular office?

options.text: It gives greater privacy to each worker
It makes supervision of staff easier and saves space
It prevents the spread of information among workers

mcq.explanation: Because all staff share one room, the supervisor can see everyone easily and the firm saves on walls and floor space, though privacy is reduced.

mcq.questionText: What is meant by a 'paperless office'?

options.text: An office with no workers at all
An office that uses electronic systems so that most information is handled without paper
An office that has run out of paper
An office that does not keep any records

mcq.explanation: A paperless office uses computers, email and electronic storage to handle and keep information, greatly reducing the use of paper documents.

mcq.questionText: Why is good filing important to a business office?

options.text: It increases the amount of paper used
It allows documents to be stored safely and found quickly when needed
It removes the need for any office staff
It makes the office look untidy

mcq.explanation: Proper filing keeps records safe, in order and easy to retrieve, saving time and protecting important documents from loss or damage.

mcq.questionText: Which office worker mainly takes dictation, types letters, arranges appointments and keeps the manager's records?
mcq.explanation: A secretary handles correspondence, takes dictation, types documents, arranges the manager's appointments and keeps records confidential.

mcq.questionText: When handling outgoing mail, which of the following is the correct step before posting business letters?

options.text: Opening the envelopes to read the contents
Folding, enclosing, sealing, addressing and stamping or franking the letters
Filing the letters in the registry permanently
Throwing the letters away after typing

mcq.explanation: Outgoing mail is folded, placed in envelopes, sealed, correctly addressed and then stamped or franked before being recorded and posted.

mcq.questionText: Which of the following best describes the importance of an office to a trader in Tanzania?

options.text: It is the centre that coordinates and controls the activities of the business
It only stores goods waiting to be sold
It is used only for keeping money
It has no value to a modern business

mcq.explanation: The office acts as the nerve centre where information is processed and decisions are coordinated, helping the business run smoothly and efficiently.

fib.questionText: The place where information is received, recorded, processed, stored and supplied is called an _____.
fib.explanation: An office is the centre where all clerical and information work of a business is carried out.

fib.questionText: An office that consists of one large room shared by many workers is called an open-plan or _____ office.
fib.explanation: An open-plan office is also called a general office because all staff work together in one large room.

fib.questionText: Small separate rooms used by individuals or small groups of workers form what is called a _____ office.
fib.explanation: A cellular (private) office uses small separate rooms, giving each worker or group privacy.

fib.questionText: The office machine that prints postage marks on envelopes instead of using stamps is called a _____ machine.
fib.explanation: A franking machine prints the value of postage directly onto envelopes, replacing postage stamps.

fib.questionText: Filing documents in order of their numbers, such as invoice 001, 002, 003, is known as _____ filing.
fib.explanation: Numerical filing arranges records by number, which is useful for invoices, receipts and account numbers.

fib.questionText: The office worker who carries messages, letters and parcels from one office to another is called a _____.
fib.explanation: A messenger delivers internal and external mail, documents and small parcels within and outside the office.

fib.questionText: The department that receives, records and distributes all incoming and outgoing mail is called the _____.
fib.explanation: The registry (or mailing department) is responsible for handling and keeping records of all correspondence.

fib.questionText: Arranging documents according to topics such as 'Salaries', 'Loans' and 'Customers' is called _____ filing.
fib.explanation: Subject filing groups documents by topic or subject matter rather than by name, number or date.

fib.questionText: An office that uses computers and electronic systems to handle information with very little paper is called a _____ office.
fib.explanation: A paperless office relies on electronic storage, email and computers instead of paper records.

fib.questionText: The piece of furniture with drawers used to keep files and documents safely is called a filing _____.
fib.explanation: A filing cabinet has drawers in which files are stored in an orderly and secure way.

tf.questionText: An office is responsible for receiving, recording, processing, storing and supplying information in an organisation.
tf.explanation: These are the main functions of an office that make it the information centre of a business.

tf.questionText: A cellular office gives workers more privacy than an open-plan office.
tf.explanation: Because a cellular office uses separate rooms, each worker enjoys more privacy and quietness.

tf.questionText: A photocopier is used to send letters through the post office.
tf.explanation: A photocopier is used to make copies of documents; sending letters by post is done through the postal service or a franking machine for postage.

tf.questionText: In alphabetical filing, documents are arranged according to the letters of the alphabet from A to Z.
tf.explanation: Alphabetical filing orders records by names of persons, firms or subjects in A to Z sequence.

tf.questionText: The receptionist is usually the last person a visitor meets before leaving the office.
tf.explanation: The receptionist is normally the first person a visitor meets on arrival, creating the first impression of the organisation.

tf.questionText: Good filing helps an office to keep records safely and find them quickly when needed.
tf.explanation: Proper filing protects documents and makes retrieval fast, saving time and avoiding loss of records.

tf.questionText: A franking machine is used to store confidential files instead of a filing cabinet.
tf.explanation: A franking machine prints postage on envelopes; files are stored in filing cabinets or electronically.

tf.questionText: The registry deals with both incoming and outgoing mail of an organisation.
tf.explanation: The registry receives, records, sorts and distributes incoming mail and prepares and records outgoing mail.

tf.questionText: A paperless office aims to reduce the use of paper by using electronic systems.
tf.explanation: A paperless office uses computers, email and electronic storage so that most information is handled without paper.

tf.questionText: Geographical filing arranges documents according to the dates on which they were received.
tf.explanation: Geographical filing arranges records by place such as region or town; arranging by date is chronological filing.

summary.questionText: State two main functions of an office.
summary.correctAnswer: Receiving and recording information; processing, storing and supplying information.
summary.explanation: An office collects information, keeps records, processes them and supplies the results to those who need them.

summary.questionText: Give two differences between an open-plan office and a cellular office.
summary.correctAnswer: An open-plan office uses one large shared room and makes supervision easy but offers little privacy, while a cellular office uses separate small rooms giving more privacy but is harder to supervise and uses more space.
summary.explanation: The two office types differ mainly in privacy, space use and ease of supervision.

summary.questionText: Mention three types of office machines or equipment found in a modern office.
summary.correctAnswer: Computers, printers, photocopiers, telephones, filing cabinets and franking machines (any three).
summary.explanation: Modern offices use such machines to process, copy, communicate and store information efficiently.

summary.questionText: List four methods of filing used in an office.
summary.correctAnswer: Alphabetical, numerical, geographical, chronological and subject filing (any four).
summary.explanation: These methods arrange documents by name, number, place, date or topic so they can be retrieved easily.

summary.questionText: State two duties of an office secretary.
summary.correctAnswer: Taking dictation and typing letters; arranging the manager's appointments and keeping records.
summary.explanation: A secretary handles correspondence, scheduling and record keeping for the manager.

summary.questionText: Explain the importance of filing in an office.
summary.correctAnswer: Filing keeps documents safe, in order and easy to find quickly, saves time, prevents loss or damage of records and provides evidence and reference for future use.
summary.explanation: Effective filing protects information and makes it readily available when required.

summary.questionText: Describe the steps in handling incoming mail in an office.
summary.correctAnswer: Receive and sort the mail, open the envelopes, date-stamp the letters, record them in the inward register, and distribute them to the relevant officers or departments.
summary.explanation: Incoming mail must be received, recorded and passed to the right person promptly and accurately.

summary.questionText: Give three duties of an office messenger.
summary.correctAnswer: Carrying letters and documents between offices, delivering and collecting mail at the post office, and running errands such as taking parcels to clients.
summary.explanation: A messenger handles the movement of documents and small items within and outside the office.

summary.questionText: State two advantages of using modern technology such as computers in the office.
summary.correctAnswer: It speeds up work and processing of information, and it allows large amounts of information to be stored and retrieved easily with fewer errors.
summary.explanation: Computers improve speed, accuracy and storage of information, supporting the paperless office.

summary.questionText: Explain what is meant by records management in an office.
summary.correctAnswer: Records management is the process of creating, organising, storing, retrieving, protecting and disposing of an organisation's records in a systematic way so that needed information is available and unwanted records are removed.
summary.explanation: Good records management ensures information is well kept throughout its life and easily accessed when required.

hoq.questionText: A growing supermarket in Mwanza has branches in several regions and keeps thousands of supplier records. The manager wants records grouped by region first, then by supplier name within each region. Which filing approach best suits this need?

options.text: Chronological filing only, by date of supply
Geographical filing by region, with alphabetical arrangement of suppliers within each region
Numerical filing only, by random file numbers
Subject filing by type of goods only

hoq.explanation: Because records must be grouped by region and then by name, a geographical method combined with alphabetical order within each region meets both requirements.

hoq.questionText: A company in Dar es Salaam sends out hundreds of letters every day and the cost and time of sticking postage stamps has become a problem. Which combination of measures would most improve the handling of its outgoing mail?

options.text: Stop sending letters and keep all documents unposted
Use a franking machine for postage and adopt email for suitable correspondence to cut paper and time
Buy more filing cabinets to store the letters
Employ more receptionists to greet visitors

hoq.explanation: A franking machine speeds up stamping and controls postage costs, while using email for appropriate letters reduces paper and delivery time, directly solving the outgoing mail problem.

hoq.questionText: A small firm in Arusha has frequent loss of documents, slow service to visitors and poor supervision of clerks who work in scattered rooms. As an office consultant, which single change would best address all three problems at once?

options.text: Adopt an open-plan layout with a proper reception desk and a well-organised filing and records system
Remove the filing cabinets and rely on workers' memory
Close the reception and let visitors find offices on their own
Give each clerk a separate locked room with no shared records

hoq.explanation: An open-plan layout improves supervision, a reception desk speeds visitor service, and an organised filing and records system reduces document loss, tackling all three problems together.
